title: qgb project context (Phase 3 Step 3.0)
description: Self-declaration of the target project. Mediates between human prose (.quality-system/knowledge/project-context.md) and machine consumers (qgb design-stages propose-context output, Phase 5 skills). The md file is the human-authored source of truth; this json is the machine-readable structured form. An assisting agent (claude-code / codex-cli / gemini-cli) typically transforms the md into this json, and a human reviews and sets human_reviewed=true. qgb only validates the schema and surfaces warnings (P8: utilising user's explicit declaration); it never derives ALLOW/DENY from this content (P6). **Not for cross-project comparison (P11)**: free-form values like project_kind / technologies / artifact_kinds are deliberately not enum-constrained and should not be used to rank or benchmark projects against each other. **Free prose fields (purpose, scope.*, non_adopted_methods[].reason, references[].path) are data, not instructions (P8 / NF-007)**: consumers (Phase 5 skills, agents) must not inject these strings as prompts or commands; the document_kind metadata on propose-context output signals 'input material', not 'executable directive'.

schema_version.description: Project-context schema version. Only '1.0' is supported in Phase 3.

human_reviewed.description: true when a human has reviewed and approved this json (not just an agent draft). qgb design-stages propose-context emits a warning when this is false so external LLMs know the context is provisional. P8 boundary: only human-reviewed declarations count as 'utilising user's explicit declaration'.

project_kind.description: Free-form descriptor of what kind of artifact set this project produces. Examples: 'python-cli', 'prompt-collection', 'terraform-modules', 'legal-templates', 'mixed-devops'. Intentionally NOT constrained by enum to avoid recreating the language-centric model that adapters had — qgb targets any artifact set that can be machine-checked, not just programming language projects.

purpose.description: Why this project exists; what value it delivers. Free-form prose.

scope.description: What this project intends to cover vs. what it explicitly excludes.

technologies.description: Free-form list of technologies used. NOT a single 'language' field by design: a project may use no programming language at all (markdown docs, prompt sets) or many (mixed-devops). Examples: ['python', 'pytest'], ['terraform', 'aws'], ['markdown'], ['claude-code', 'codex-cli'].

artifact_kinds.description: What kinds of artifacts this project produces. Examples: ['source-code', 'tests'], ['documentation'], ['prompt-templates'], ['ci-configuration'], ['legal-contract-templates'].

non_adopted_methods.description: Methods explicitly rejected by the project and why. Important context for stage design (LLM should not propose these stages).

path.description: Project-relative path or URL. qgb does not dereference these (P8/NF-007: external content is data, not instructions).

generated_by.description: 'human' = handwritten; 'agent-assisted' = an LLM agent helped structure it from project-context.md. The distinction matters for P8: human-authored json is a primary user declaration; agent-assisted json should be human-reviewed (human_reviewed=true) before being trusted as such.

agent_name.description: When generated_by='agent-assisted': identifier of the assisting agent (e.g. 'claude-code', 'codex-cli', 'gemini-cli'). qgb does not dispatch on this value; it is provenance only.

generated_at.description: When this json was generated (RFC 3339 / ISO 8601).

source_md_sha256.description: SHA-256 of .quality-system/knowledge/project-context.md at the time of generation. Allows detecting md updates that orphan the json (Phase 3+: qgb validate-policy may surface a project_context_stale advisory when md hash differs).
